Terminos.title: Terms and conditions
Terminos.legalNote: This document describes clearly how the Radar IA service works and under what conditions we offer it. It does not replace legal advice — since we operate in several LATAM countries with different legal frameworks, consult a lawyer if you need a version with formal legal standing for your country.
Terminos.serviceBody: Radar IA is an audit and monitoring service for business visibility in AI engine answers (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity). We run real questions related to your industry and city against those engines, measure whether and how your business is mentioned, audit technical and content factors that influence that visibility, and — on paid plans — repeat the measurement on a regular basis.
Terminos.accountsBody: To use the free audit we ask for your WhatsApp and email; we verify the WhatsApp number with a one-time code before showing you the report. Creating a paid-plan account additionally requires an email and password. You're responsible for keeping your password confidential and for the accuracy of the business information you give us.
Terminos.freeAuditBody: The free audit runs a short version (fewer questions) of the same real measurement engine used by paid plans — it is not a simulation or a made-up result. We apply reasonable usage limits (by phone, domain, and IP) to prevent abuse of the service; if we detect an automated or fraudulent usage pattern, we may suspend access.
Terminos.billingBody: Paid plans have a one-time setup cost and a recurring fee, shown in your local currency before you pay. Payments are processed through Stripe — we do not store your card details. The Enterprise plan has custom pricing, quoted directly with you. You can cancel the recurring subscription at any time; the setup cost, being work already performed, is non-refundable unless the law applicable in your country states otherwise.
Terminos.guaranteeTitle: What we guarantee and what we don't
Terminos.guaranteeBody: We cannot control which business an AI recommends — neither OpenAI, Anthropic, nor Google offer that guarantee in their own systems, so neither do we. What we do guarantee is that the measurement we show you is the real result of querying those engines (not an estimate), and that the audit and fix work is performed on verifiable information about your business.
Terminos.ownershipTitle: Ownership of information and the report
Terminos.ownershipBody: You keep ownership of your business's information. The report and analysis we generate are for your use — you can share them however you like. We retain the technical and measurement data needed to operate the service (score history, findings, questions used) while your account is active.
Terminos.acceptableUseBody: You may not use the service to audit other businesses without authorization for harassment or unfair-competition purposes, attempt to evade the system's usage or rate limits, or use internal APIs outside their intended purpose. We reserve the right to suspend accounts that abuse the service or put its availability for other users at risk.
Terminos.cancellationBody: You can cancel your subscription anytime from your dashboard or by contacting us; cancellation applies at the next billing cycle. Once cancelled, we stop running new measurements, but we keep your history for a reasonable period in case you want to reactivate.
Terminos.changesBody: We may update these terms as the product evolves. If a change is material, we'll notify you by email or WhatsApp before it takes effect.
Terminos.lawBody: Since Radar IA operates in several LATAM countries (Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Peru, Argentina, and Brazil), the applicable law and jurisdiction for disputes is determined by your country of residence and the specific contract you signed, if any. For the Enterprise plan, these details are agreed directly in the quote.
Terminos.contactBody: If you have questions about these terms, write to us through the same WhatsApp or email you used for your account.

Privacidad.title: Data policy
Privacidad.legalNote: This document describes, clearly and based on what the product actually does, what data we collect and how we use it. It does not replace legal advice — since we operate in several LATAM countries with different data protection laws (e.g. LGPD in Brazil or Mexico's Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data), consult a lawyer if you need a version with formal legal standing for your country.
Privacidad.dataCollectedBody: Business name, industry, city, and country; WhatsApp phone number and email; website or app-store listing, depending on the business type; tax ID, only if you sign up for a paid plan. We don't collect payment data directly — Stripe processes that. We also don't collect personal data about your own business's customers: the questions we audit are generic to your industry and city (e.g. "what's a good [industry] in [city]?"), and contain no third-party information.
Privacidad.howWeUseBody: To run the visibility audit (query the AI engines, audit your site, calculate your score), verify your identity via a WhatsApp code, process payments and billing, send you your report and account-related notifications, and prevent abuse of the service (usage limits, automated-pattern detection).
Privacidad.sharingBody: Stripe, to process payments. Meta (WhatsApp Business API), to send the verification code and notifications. Resend, to send emails. Supabase and Vercel, as infrastructure providers (database and hosting). We do not sell your data to third parties or use it for advertising.
Privacidad.aiEnginesBody: To measure your visibility, we send generic questions about your industry and city to the OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), and Perplexity APIs, and record their public answer. These questions don't include personal data about you or your customers — they're generic search-intent questions, the same kind anyone could ask those engines.
Privacidad.securityBody: We apply row-level access control in the database (each business can only read its own information), encrypted connections, rate limits on public endpoints, and standard security headers. No system is perfectly secure, but we treat your information with the same practices we use to protect our own.
Privacidad.cookiesBody: We use a cookie to remember your preferred language (Spanish, English, or Portuguese) and the session cookies needed to keep you signed in if you have an account. We don't use advertising tracking cookies.
Privacidad.retentionBody: We keep your information while your account is active. If you cancel or stop using the free audit, we keep a reasonable history in case you come back, but you can ask us to delete your data at any time (see the next section).
Privacidad.rightsBody: You can ask us to access, correct, or delete your data by writing to us through the WhatsApp or email tied to your account. Depending on your country, you may have additional rights under local data protection law — we honor those to the extent the applicable law requires.
Privacidad.changesBody: If we materially change what data we collect or how we use it, we'll notify you before the change takes effect.
Privacidad.contactBody: For any request related to your data, write to us through the same WhatsApp or email you used for your account.

ComoFunciona.title: How Radar IA works
ComoFunciona.hook: From the question to the fix: here's the full path, from the first audit to month-over-month monitoring.
ComoFunciona.step1Body: We run the questions your customers actually ask ("what's a good [industry] in [city]?", "best options for...", etc.) against ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity in real time — we don't simulate or guess the answer, we actually query it. The free audit uses a short version (5 questions); paid plans run the full question set for your industry.
ComoFunciona.step2Title: 2. We show the evidence, not an opinion
ComoFunciona.step2Body: For every question we show you whether you were mentioned, which source the engine cited, and why (or why not). We also audit 8 technical and content factors that predict whether an AI can find you and trust your information: name/address/phone consistency, your Google Business profile (or catalog if you sell online), whether your site allows AI crawlers, structured data, coverage of frequent questions, presence in directories and press, reviews, and the real result of direct measurement.
ComoFunciona.step3Title: 3. We prioritize what to fix first
ComoFunciona.step3Body: Not every finding carries the same weight — a crawler block that makes you invisible isn't the same as one extra review. The fix plan ranks findings by severity and real impact on your score, so you know exactly what to move first.
ComoFunciona.step4Body: Fixing something once isn't enough — AI engines change their answers over time. Every paid plan re-runs the full measurement on a fixed cadence (monthly, biweekly, weekly, or daily on Enterprise), so your score and evidence stay current, not a single snapshot from signup day.
ComoFunciona.pillarsBody: Each factor has a weight validated with real data (not a made-up number) on how much it influences whether an AI recommends you. They add up to 100%.
ComoFunciona.axesBody: The 8 factors adapt to how you sell: local or service business, online store, or mobile/digital app. The underlying logic is the same — only what counts as "your listing" and "your reputation" changes.
ComoFunciona.cadenceBody: The difference between plans is mostly how many questions get measured and how often re-measurement runs — the scoring method is exactly the same across all of them.

QueEsGeo.title: What is GEO? AI engine optimization, explained simply
QueEsGeo.hook: GEO, AEO, "AI visibility" — new terms for a real problem: getting ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Perplexity to mention your business when someone asks them something in your industry.
QueEsGeo.q1: What does GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) mean?
QueEsGeo.a1: GEO is the set of practices for making your business the source an AI cites or recommends when someone asks it something related to your industry. Unlike traditional SEO, which aims to show up in a list of links, GEO aims to make your business the answer itself, not one result among ten.
QueEsGeo.q2: Are GEO and AEO the same thing?
QueEsGeo.a2: They're used almost as synonyms. AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) emphasizes the AI answering directly by citing your business without anyone having to click anything; GEO is the broader term for optimizing content for generative engines. In practice, the techniques overlap almost completely.
QueEsGeo.q3: Does this replace the SEO I already know?
QueEsGeo.a3: No, it complements it. Generative AI engines — ChatGPT especially — rely heavily on traditional search indexes to answer with up-to-date information, so ranking well there still matters. What's new is that you now also have to think about direct-answer content, structured data, and getting mentioned by other sites, not just keywords.
QueEsGeo.q4: How does Radar IA measure this in practice?
QueEsGeo.a4: With 8 real pillars, not a single metric: from the consistency of your business identity to whether AI engines actually mention you when we ask them on your behalf — with real evidence from each response, not a guess.

ComoAparecerChatGPT.title: How to get ChatGPT to recommend your business
ComoAparecerChatGPT.hook: The question we get asked most. Short answer: there are no paid shortcuts, but there are real factors you can work on.
ComoAparecerChatGPT.q1: Can I pay to get ChatGPT to recommend me?
ComoAparecerChatGPT.a1: No. Unlike search or social media advertising, there's no paid scheme for appearing in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini's organic answers — no company, including ours, can guarantee you a mention in exchange for money. What does exist is working on the real factors those engines use to decide who to mention.
ComoAparecerChatGPT.q2: What factors do AI engines use to decide who to mention?
ComoAparecerChatGPT.a2: In short: your identity being consistent across the web, your site having structured data (schema) an AI can read without ambiguity, having content that directly answers real questions, and other sites (reviews, directories, press, forums) mentioning you — the more your name shows up next to your industry's key phrases, the better.
ComoAparecerChatGPT.q3: Do I need to be indexed on Google or Bing?
ComoAparecerChatGPT.a3: Both matter, but Bing especially: ChatGPT uses Bing's index for its real-time web searches, so if your site isn't indexed there, it's harder to get cited — many businesses never verified their site on Bing Webmaster Tools simply because nobody told them to.
ComoAparecerChatGPT.q4: How long does it take to see a change?
ComoAparecerChatGPT.a4: Honestly: there's no fixed number, and be wary of anyone who gives you one. Generative AI engines don't publish how or when they update what they "know" about a brand. What you can measure right away are the controllable factors — actually showing up in answers is the consequence of improving those, not something you can force directly.

RadarVsMentio.a1: It's a tool that also generates native-language questions by industry and market, and measures brand mentions across several AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity). It has a limited free plan and paid plans starting at roughly US$29/month (reference price as of when this was written — it may change, confirm on their site).
RadarVsMentio.a2: Radar IA is built specifically for Latin American businesses: prices you see in your own currency at checkout (not just dollars), a bank of tens of thousands of real questions written country by country and city by city — not generic translations of English-language templates — and an 8-pillar system that also audits the controllable technical and content factors, not just mention measurement.
RadarVsMentio.q3: Which one covers more countries or languages?
RadarVsMentio.a3: We don't have verified data on Mentio's exact country coverage, so we won't invent a comparison there. What we can tell you for certain: Radar IA is actively building, country by country, a bank of native Spanish and Portuguese questions across Latin America — not a generic translation of an English-language set.
RadarVsMentio.a4: Sure, they're not mutually exclusive. Our honest recommendation: try Radar IA's free audit first — it's the only way to compare with real data from your own business instead of just comparing feature lists in a table like this one.

CuantoCuestaIA.title: How much does it cost to measure a brand's AI visibility?
CuantoCuestaIA.hook: An honest look at 2026 market pricing, and where Radar IA fits in.
CuantoCuestaIA.q1: How much do AI visibility tools charge?
CuantoCuestaIA.a1: It varies a lot by tool: there are options from about US$20-29/month up to US$250-295/month for the ones aimed at large enterprises, with some charging by credits or queries instead of a flat fee. These are reference prices from the international market as of when this was written — always confirm on each provider's site, since they change often.
CuantoCuestaIA.q2: Why do most of them charge in dollars?
CuantoCuestaIA.a2: Because they're built by and for the English-speaking US/EU market. As things stand, that means a business in Mexico or Colombia pays the same dollar rate as a company in New York, with no adjustment for local purchasing power.
CuantoCuestaIA.q3: How does Radar IA's pricing work?
CuantoCuestaIA.a3: It's shown in your local currency at checkout, with automatic conversion — there's no hidden flat dollar rate behind it. The initial audit is always free and doesn't ask for a card.
CuantoCuestaIA.q4: Is it worth paying for this yet?
CuantoCuestaIA.a4: It depends on how much your customers rely on asking an AI before deciding. If your industry and city already have real volume of that kind of query, measuring it gives you concrete evidence instead of flying blind; if you're not sure, the free audit shows you that with no commitment before you pay anything.
